script.analysis: All 20,636 stored characters read in two contiguous ranges with canonical hash match. Hook: 2 a.m. bank check made calmer by $1,000/month passive income; subscribe CTA. Claims: $1K/month crosses an "anxiety threshold"; covers basic needs in many places; behavioral benefits (negotiating, risk-taking). Routes: ~$300K at 4% dividend yield, $60K down on a $300K short-term rental, digital/affiliate income with little capital. Reinvestment: $12K/year at 8% for 13 years -> ~$250K -> ~$860/month at 4%; warnings about lifestyle inflation; year-by-year growth path ($1,200, $1,500, $2,500 at year 5, $5-8K at year 10); opportunity cost "$300 of assets per $1 of monthly spending"; multiple streams and abundance; lifestyle creep; nervous-system framing; wealthy families inherit buffer psychology; close. Long, repetitive motivational content; few sources; key growth arithmetic overstated. No community CTA. ASR not audio-verified.

claim_audit: 0:10300 $1,000/month at a 4% yield requires $300,000 - correct. $12,000/year reinvested at 8% for 13 years = ~$258,000; 4% of $250K = $10,000/year (~$833/month) - consistent with "~$860". "Psychologists call it the anxiety threshold" and "studies show modest passive income changes career/risk choices" are unsourced. $60K down on a $300K short-term rental producing $1K/month "passive" income is optimistic and operationally active. "Reinvesting $1,000 every month adds $300,000 worth of purchasing power to your portfolio every single year" is wrong: reinvestment adds $12,000/year of principal; $300K is the capital needed to generate $1K/month.

10300:20636 Growth path overstated: reinvesting $1K/month from a $300K base at ~8% total return yields ~$1,080/month in year 1, ~$1,470 by year 5 and ~$2,160 by year 10 at a 4% payout - not $2,500 at year 5 or $5,000-8,000 at year 10 "without adding a single dollar". Opportunity cost framed as "$300 of assets per $1 of monthly spending" equates spending passive income with destroying the capital that produces it. "$1,000 is ~3 months of bare-bones survival money" contradicts the earlier claim that it covers a month of basic needs. "Pathway from $1K to $10K is much shorter than 0 to $1K" is unsupported.
